sections.h2: What are the address and hours of the Wilkes County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office sits at 500 Court House Drive, Suite 1000, Wilkesboro, NC 28697. Call 336-651-7351 or fax 336-990-0041. Doors are open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:55 p.m., closed on holidays, according to the county page.

Tax Administration is in a different building, the Wilkes County Offices at 110 North Street. A Wilkesboro seller may need both, or can have an attorney record while phoning the tax office for figures.

  • Land records: Court House Drive, Suite 1000
  • Tax bills and appeals: North Street
  • Recording deadline for the day: 4:55 p.m.

Call ahead on a closing day if the packet runs long, since pages past the first fifteen of a deed add to the charge.

sections.h2: How old are Wilkes County land records?
sections.html:
They begin with the formation of the county in 1778. Birth and death records start in 1913, with a few earlier delayed birth entries, and marriage licenses go back to 1882.

The register lists deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, plats, separation agreements, foreclosures, notary oaths and military discharges among the papers it takes in. Digitizing is ongoing, so ask the office how far back a given book is indexed.

For a parcel with deep family ownership, older deeds can describe land by landmarks instead of lot numbers. A survey tied to the current deed saves arguments with a buyer's title examiner.

Heirs sorting an estate often start here, since births, deaths and marriages are on file alongside land records. A short visit with the death certificate and the last recorded deed can show who held title and whether a loan was ever released.

sections.h2: Where can I search Wilkes County deeds online?
sections.html:
At wilkesncrod.org, which the register of deeds opened on July 1, 2017. That is the authoritative site for recorded documents.

The tax office runs a second, narrower tool. Its Deed Search holds face pages and legal descriptions of certain deeds that the tax office scanned for its mapping staff. Signature and notary pages are usually left off, and deeds of trust, satisfactions and wills are not included.

The disclaimer tells attorneys and title examiners not to rely on it. Treat it as a quick way to find a legal description by book and page, and use the register for the real record.

The tax office tool works by book and page. Once you have those numbers from a prior deed or from the register's own site, you can pull the scanned face page and compare its legal description with your survey. Keep a printout for your attorney.

sections.h2: What are the Wilkes County recording charges?
sections.html:
Recording charges under G.S. 161-10, as collected in Wilkes County
FilingCharge
Deed, general instrument$26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 through page 35, then $4.00 a page
Loan releaseNo charge
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Extra instrument within one document$10.00 each

The statute says these are the only fees, payable before filing. Ask at the counter what your packet will cost.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed tax on a Wilkes County sale?
sections.html:
The seller does, at the register of deeds, before recording. The statute puts it at one dollar per five hundred dollars or part of the value of the interest conveyed (G.S. 105-228.30).

The county general fund keeps half. The balance goes to the state monthly, less refunds and an allowance.

sections.h2: How does recording protect a Wilkes County buyer?
sections.html:
A deed that is not registered loses to lien creditors and later buyers who paid value, and priority follows the time of registration (G.S. 47-18). Lawyers therefore record on the day funds move.

  • Locate paid off loans and confirm releases are on record
  • Get the tax balance from North Street
  • Bring the excise tax with the deed
  • Record the deed ahead of the buyer's loan

The register is elected by county voters (G.S. 161-1).

sections.h2: What if a Wilkes County tract has boundary questions?
sections.html:
State law lets a person gain title by 20 years of possession under known and visible lines and boundaries, adverse to others (G.S. 1-40). On older rural tracts, fences and farm roads may sit off the deed line.

Before listing, pull the vesting deed from the register, order a survey if lines are unclear, and tell your attorney about any neighbor who uses part of the land. A buyer's examiner will find recorded claims, so surprises cost more late.

sections.h2: How should a Wilkes County owner prepare before closing day?
sections.html:
Work backward from the recording desk. The register closes at 4:55 p.m., so a closing that wraps up at four leaves little room for a corrected page.

  • Ask your attorney who will carry the package to Court House Drive, or whether it goes electronically.
  • Check that every signature and notary stamp is complete.
  • Have a check ready for the filing charge if the closing office does not cover it.
  • Keep the recorded copy, with its book and page, for your files.

The book and page numbers are what the tax office's deed search asks for, so they also help later when you need a legal description for a survey or an insurance form.

sections.h2: How did the 2025 revaluation change what Wilkes sellers record?
sections.html:
The county estimated that real property values rose about 75% to 80% overall as of January 1, 2025, with ranges that varied from town to town, in its revaluation release.

For recording, the price in the contract is what matters for the excise tax. The tax value does not set it. If your contract price and the county's value differ widely, your attorney can explain why before the deed is drafted.

The release also says the county reappraises more often than the eight year minimum. Check with the tax office for the schedule.

sections.h2: Where should a Wilkes County seller go for each document?
sections.html:
A short map prevents trips to the wrong building.

  • Deeds, deeds of trust, plats, powers of attorney, foreclosure papers: Register of Deeds, Court House Drive
  • Tax balances, appeals, relief applications, parcel and GIS look-ups: Tax Administration, North Street
  • Court files, estates and wills: Clerk of Superior Court

The deed search page itself points to the register and the clerk of superior court for any authoritative use of land records. Keep the three straight and a sale usually moves without a second visit.

sections.h2: What other Wilkesboro records come up in a sale?
sections.html:
Besides deeds, the register takes foreclosure papers and powers of attorney, which matter when an owner signs by proxy or the lender has begun sale proceedings. The county also lets people look up parcels through the tax office's real property search and GIS maps.

If you want to confirm who is on the tax record, search the parcel there, then match it to the recorded deed at wilkesncrod.org. Mismatches usually trace to an unrecorded transfer or a name change.

  • Real property search on the tax site
  • GIS parcel maps
  • Recorded deed at wilkesncrod.org

faqs.q: When does the Wilkes County Register of Deeds close?
faqs.a: At 4:55 p.m., Monday through Friday. The doors open at 8:30 a.m. and close for holidays.

faqs.q: How can I search Wilkes County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Use wilkesncrod.org, the register's site that has been online since July 1, 2017. The tax office also has a limited deed copy tool for finding legal descriptions.

faqs.q: What year do Wilkes County land records start?
faqs.a: 1778, when the county was formed. Births and deaths begin in 1913, and marriage licenses in 1882.

faqs.q: Do I pay to record a loan release in Wilkes County?
faqs.a: No. The statewide fee schedule sets no charge for a satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust.

faqs.q: Who owes the excise tax on a Wilkes County deed?
faqs.a: The seller. It is paid to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.
